ai.description: *Sitana gokakensis* is a small agamid reaching 50–60 mm SVL. It features a brownish body with a dark vertebral stripe and a distinct, tri-colored (blue, black, red) gular fan in breeding males.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sitana gokakensis* is best distinguished by its unique, multi-colored throat fan (dewlap) that features distinct blue, black, and red patches, unlike the simpler patterns of other *Sitana* species.
ai.habitat: *Sitana gokakensis* inhabits semi-arid, rocky grasslands and scrublands in the Deccan Plateau, typically found at elevations between 500 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, males perform conspicuous displays by rapidly extending and retracting a brightly colored throat fan to attract mates and deter rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sitana gokakensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs annually during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sitana gokakensis* is endemic to the Deccan Plateau in northern Karnataka, India, specifically inhabiting rocky, scrub-covered landscapes near Gokak at low elevations.
